claspgroup-clasp-group:ashbyhq:cd04df78-.description: Business Development Rep Location Open to Remote in ET or CT Locations ONLY About Us Clasp is a mission-driven, venture-backed startup transforming access to education and career pathways—starting with the healthcare workforce. By enabling employers to invest in future talent where it matters most—easing overwhelming student debt—our platform creates lasting bonds between employers and employees. We believe that when employers have a stake in the cost of education, we can create a more sustainable, equitable, and skilled workforce. Fresh off our Series B, we’re entering our next phase of growth. Clasp is a Forbes Fintech 50 company, an SHRM portfolio company, and has been named by Business Insider as one of the “Top 14 Healthcare Startups to Watch in 2026” and one of the “43 Startups to Bet Your Career On in 2025.” We’re not just building a fintech product—we’re driving economic mobility. If you’re excited to build, grow, and make a real impact, join us. What We Need The Business Development Rep at Clasp is responsible for building relationships with Universities to develop deep partnerships and build awareness for Clasp. You'll build and manage a portfolio of school and program partnerships — engaging program directors, career services contacts, and financial aid offices to secure active, ongoing communication of Clasp opportunities to their students. This is a true high-volume sales job: 60% of time to be spent on cold outreach, and 40% on building/developing/nurturing existing relationships – with clear weekly and quarterly targets. You'll spend most of your time on the phone and in virtual meetings with school contacts, managing a pipeline of partner institutions from first outreach through active distribution. The role is also up to 40% travel - with the expectation that you’ll go visit schools in person to meet with administrators and students, as well as attend career fairs. There is also a requirement to travel to full company meet ups 3x per year. What You’ll Do - Conduct one-on-one calls with school administrators, program directors, and career services contacts per week - Execute daily outbound outreach to schools and programs (calls, email sequences, follow-ups) to build new distribution partnerships, resulting in a targeted number of new applicants sourced per week - Create plans with schools to share Clasp opportunities with their students and follow through to confirmed distribution - Execute campus visits, career fairs and virtual lunch & learns - Secure testimonials per quarter from satisfied partner institutions - Explore deep, creative partnerships with schools to build a strong foundation for Clasp pathways - Maintain accurate records of all school and student interactions in CRM, tracking commitment status and distribution evidence - Partner with Marketing to develop role-based assets (landing pages, co-branded materials, social graphics) that improve school distribution and student conversion - Report on outreach activity, pipeline health, and application volume on a regular basis What You’ll Need - Scrappy, resilient, positive attitude - 2–3+ years of experience in outreach, business development, partnerships, or higher-ed engagement - Comfort with high-volume outreach and structured follow-up (calling + sequencing) - Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including storytelling and persuasion / sales skills - Strong relationship-building skills with school administrators, program directors, and career services contacts - Organized and data-fluent: able to use CRM dashboards to prioritize work, track outcomes, and report clearly - Familiarity with HubSpot or similar CRM - Experience partnering with marketing teams on conversion-driving assets and messaging What We Give In Return - Execute in vivo mouse studies, including disease model development, dosing, tissue collection, and phenotypic characterization. Develop and apply siRNA-based approaches for target validation, pathway interrogation, and mechanistic studies. Contribute to biomarker discovery, translational research efforts, and preclinical candidate characterization. Analyze, interpret, and present experimental findings to cross-functional teams and senior leadership. Generate technical reports, presentations, study summaries, and scientific documentation to support program advancement. Collaborate effectively with internal teams, CROs, academic collaborators, and external partners. Mentor junior scientists and contribute to a collaborative, innovative research environment. For Senior Scientist and Principal Scientist levels, provide scientific leadership, contribute to research strategy, and lead cross-functional initiatives. Maintain accurate experimental records and ensure compliance with institutional, ethical, and regulatory guidelines. Qualifications Ph.D. in Cell Biology, Genetics, Molecular Biology, Pharmacology, Immunology, Biomedical Sciences, or a related field with 6+ years of relevant experience for Senior Scientist roles; 8+ years of industry experience and demonstrated scientific leadership for Principal Scientist roles. Alternatively, an M.S. degree with substantial relevant industry experience. Demonstrated expertise in siRNA design, delivery, optimization, and functional validation. Hands-on experience with microscopy platforms, including fluorescence, confocal, live-cell, and high-content imaging systems. Strong quantitative data analysis, experimental design, and statistical analysis skills. Excellent communication, presentation, and scientific writing skills. jobgether-jobgether:lever:0f14288a-be6a-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Solutions & Communications Architect (Fractional Contract) based in Canada. This is a senior architecture role focused on designing and launching a secure, unified communications and workflow platform. You will lead the architecture from initial discovery through the delivery of a working pilot. The scope spans identity, data protection, integrations, approvals, monitoring, and auditability. You will work with AI-enabled workflows and automated systems while maintaining strong human oversight and security controls. The first month is highly hands-on and fast-paced, with a transition afterward to a lighter ongoing engagement of approximately 8 hours per week. This role offers significant autonomy and ownership, with a strong emphasis on thoughtful engineering and risk management. It is ideal for an experienced architect who can move quickly while knowing when to pause, challenge assumptions, and protect system integrity. Lead the discovery and architecture of a secure, unified communications and workflow environment connecting teams and systems with a central platform. Understand business, technical, security, and operational requirements thoroughly before designing or implementing solutions. Design end-to-end architectures covering identity verification, access controls, data protection, integrations, system connectivity, monitoring, and audit trails. Establish approval checkpoints and human-in-the-loop controls to ensure sensitive communications, actions, and data transfers are properly reviewed before execution. Build and launch a functional pilot within the initial intensive delivery period, including monitoring, backup plans, validation processes, and evidence that the solution operates as intended. Review technical work and deliverables from team members, identifying security, quality, architectural, or completeness concerns and redirecting work when necessary. Document architectural decisions, assumptions, risks, security considerations, and recommended next steps to support long-term scalability and governance. Support the continued maintenance, optimization, and expansion of the platform during the ongoing fractional engagement. Evaluate AI-assisted analysis and design outputs critically, ensuring automated recommendations are independently validated before being incorporated into production solutions. Requirements Senior-level experience in solution architecture, enterprise architecture, integration architecture, platform architecture, security architecture, or a closely related discipline. Demonstrated experience designing and building AI-enabled workflows, case or work-management platforms, automated systems, or solutions incorporating robust audit trails. Strong knowledge of identity and access management, data protection, least-privilege principles, security controls, and secure system design. Proven experience designing secure environments for multiple clients, organizations, or user groups while maintaining strict data isolation. Experience translating ambiguous or evolving requirements into practical, secure, and scalable technical solutions. Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate research, analysis, architecture, and design while maintaining personal accountability for validating their outputs. Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical decisions, risks, and trade-offs clearly to both technical teams and non-technical executives. Ability to work with a high degree of autonomy, make sound technical judgments, and take ownership of quality and security.
